title: Session 5: Jesus in the Quran

series.title: What does the Quran say about the Bible?

opening_question: The Quran honours Jesus: born of the virgin Mary, called the Messiah and a word from God, a worker of miracles. Read its words beside the Bible's. Where do they agree, and where does the Bible say more?

steps.question: The Quran says the angels gave Mary glad tidings "of a word from him, whose name is the Messiah". What did the angel Gabriel tell Mary in Luke, and what did she ask?

facts.text: Virgin is parthenos: "a maiden". The Quran and Luke agree on Mary's question. Sale: "how shall I have a son, since a man hath not touched me?" Luke: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
Luke's angel calls the child "the Son of the Highest" and "the Son of God". The Quran's angels call him "the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary".

steps.question: Isaiah gave a sign to the house of David. What is the sign, and what does Matthew say the name Emmanuel means?

facts.text: Isaiah's word is almah: "a lass", a young woman; the King James translates it "damsel maid virgin". The Greek Septuagint, made before Christ, has parthenos, virgin, and Matthew quotes it.
Matthew explains the name: Emmanuel is "God with us".

steps.question: In the Quran Jesus speaks from the cradle: "Peace on me the day I was born, and the day I die". What are the first words of Jesus the Bible records, and how old was he?

facts.text: The Bible records no words of Jesus as a baby. His first recorded words, at twelve, speak of "my Father's business".
The speaking baby is not in the Bible. A similar story is in the Arabic Infancy Gospel, a writing outside the Bible.

steps.question: The Quran lists Jesus' miracles: healing the blind and the leper and raising the dead. What does Jesus tell John's disciples, and how did he heal the man born blind?

facts.text: Sale's Quran has Jesus "heal one blind from his birth"; John 9 tells of "a man which was blind from his birth".
The bird of clay is not in the Bible. A boy Jesus who makes sparrows of clay that fly away is in the Infancy Gospel of Thomas, a second-century writing outside the Bible.
In the Quran every miracle is "by My permission". In John, Jesus says "I must work the works of him that sent me".

steps.question: The Quran calls Jesus the Messiah. What does Messiah mean, and what did Jesus say when the woman of Samaria spoke of the Messiah?

facts.text: Messias comes from the Hebrew mashiach: "anointed". Christ is christos, the Greek word for the same thing: "anointed".

The Quran calls Jesus the Messiah (3:45, 4:171) but does not explain the title. In the Bible the Messiah is the anointed King promised to David's house, who "shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever".

steps.question: Jesus promised "another Comforter". Who is the Comforter, according to these verses, and when would he come?

facts.text: The Comforter is "the Spirit of truth", whom "the world cannot receive": "he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you". John 14:26 names him "the Holy Ghost".

Many Muslims read Quran 61:6, where Jesus speaks of a messenger to come named Ahmad, as pointing to these verses. In John the Comforter is sent to the disciples themselves, and Acts 1:5 says it would be "not many days hence".

steps.question: Living it out: the woman of Samaria left her waterpot and said "Come, see a man". What did she do with what she heard, and what did Jesus ask His disciples?

facts.text: "many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him for the saying of the woman". Jesus asked: "But whom say ye that I am?"

remember.text: The angel told Mary she "shalt call his name JESUS".
"Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us"
His first recorded words: "I must be about my Father's business".
"the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed"
To the woman of Samaria: "I that speak unto thee am he".
